chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: "Know that the beginning of the time is always the most superior, so hasten to do good as much as you can, and the most beloved of deeds to Allah, the Exalted and Mighty, is that which the servant remains upon, even if it is little."

key_terms.مَا دَامَ الْعَبْدُ عَلَيْهِ: as long as the servant remains upon it (consistency)

ai.seo_question: What is the most virtuous time for performing acts of worship according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) highlights the virtue of 'early performance' (Tasri' al-'Amal) in worship, a concept central to Shia jurisprudence regarding the optimal times for prayers. He distinguishes between the merit of timing and the merit of consistency (Istiqamah), teaching that while hastening good deeds is superior, steadfastness in even small acts is most beloved to Allah. This hadith is foundational in the chapter on prayer times, emphasizing that spiritual excellence lies in both promptness and persistence.
